summary: Fire tower on a 48-acre state towersite near Dixon, in use by 1950; a 2015 plan lists it, and its condition since is unknown.

access.note: The towersite has a locked gate at the entrance. The rest of the area is open to appropriate public use and state regulations apply.

events.note: Dixon tower radioed a fire southeast of Crocker; a Fort Leonard Wood tower cross-shot it
2015 plan: fire tower built 1956, 90 ft tall; the 1964-65 annual report describes a different tower
Major repairs to the Dixon tower (fiscal 1956-57 annual report)
Fiscal 1964-65 annual report: a 100-foot steel tower erected at the towersite
Pond constructed on the towersite (fiscal 1972-73 annual report)

notes_for_editor: Build date and height conflict. The 2015 plan gives 1956 and 90 ft. The fiscal 1964-65 annual report gives an erected 100-ft steel tower. A tower already existed by 1950 (the fire report) and had major repairs in fiscal 1956-57, so the plan's 1956 may not be the first tower. The 2015 plan is the latest source; condition and access since 2015 are not found. Not used: a Missouri Conservation History Facebook post with a historic photo (page would not load), and Wikimapia's operating-hours line (crowd-sourced). The fire-season staffing line in the 2022 article is department-wide, not specific to Dixon. The brief's status (unknown) is left as is.
